correctness.rationale: The standard support-function curvature h+h″≥0 and Fourier support-area identity transform the convexity constraint into ||X cos(nθ)+Y cos(mθ)||∞≤1 and area minimization into maximizing X²+r²Y², X=2(n²−1)a/w,Y=2(m²−1)b/w,r²=(n²−1)/(m²−1). For n∤m, sampling angles where cos(nθ)=1 yields cos(mθ) values of an odd d=n/gcd(n,m) cycle. For d=3 averaging their squares proves norm²≥X²+Y²/2; for odd d≥5 sampled extrema prove norm≥|X|+cos(π/d)|Y| (after global sign), hence norm²≥X²+κ_d²Y². The rational q≥d+2 estimate proves r²<κ_d², so objective ≤1−(κ_d²−r²)Y² with equality only Y0, |X|1. This gives exact pure-n min, unique fixed-axis equality and displayed nonsharp stability gap. For m=kn with odd k≥3, choose t=1/(k²+1), X=1+t,Y=−t. Chebyshev derivative ||T_k′||∞≤k² implies ||(1+t)x−tT_k(x)||∞≤1, but objective =1+2t+(1+r²)t²>1. This proves strict improvement for every divisible pair; does not optimize this class. Fresh exact rational independent comparison covered 2304 nondivisible pairs and four sampled divisible constructions, with analytic proof separately evaluated.
residual_risks: Sharp divisible-class minimum intentionally unknown here, despite prior exact k=3 case; the gap bound is positive but not asserted optimal. Support-function feasibility includes zero curvature at isolated directions, not strictly positive curvature.
